protected_scheduled_posts.hook: The iris is named after the Greek goddess of the rainbow, because the flower comes in almost every color.
Elephant herds are led by the oldest female. In dry seasons, she remembers where to find water.
Researchers think red foxes use Earth's magnetic field to line up their pounce when they hunt under snow.
Bees build honeycomb in hexagons because the shape holds the most honey with the least wax.
Dolphins rest one half of their brain at a time, so they can keep surfacing to breathe while they sleep.
Young sunflowers turn to follow the sun across the sky. Once they bloom, most of them settle facing east.
A single ladybug can eat thousands of aphids in its lifetime, which is why gardeners call them lucky.
The harvest mouse weighs about as much as a sugar cube, light enough to climb a single stalk of wheat.
Cherry blossoms usually last about a week on the branch, which is why people plan whole trips around them.
Nearly all calico cats are female. The orange and black in their coat are carried on the X chromosome.
The moon drifts about 3.8 centimeters farther from Earth every year.
Butterflies taste with their feet. Sensors on their legs tell them when they've landed on the right plant.
Sunlight takes about eight minutes to reach us. The sunrise you see already happened a few minutes ago.
Snakes shed their skin in one piece, often turned inside out, several times a year as they grow.
Cats can't taste sweetness. They're drawn to fish for the protein, not the flavor.
Studies show honeybees can learn to recognize human faces.
Olive trees can live for more than a thousand years, and some of the oldest still bear fruit.
Giant pandas spend about half of every day eating bamboo.
Raindrops aren't shaped like tears. Small ones are round, and larger ones flatten out as they fall.
A daisy is really hundreds of flowers in one. Each speck in the yellow center is its own tiny bloom.
Cats sleep between 12 and 16 hours a day, ideally somewhere warm.
Most of the stars you can see at night are bigger and brighter than our sun.
